# Risk strips and the Home cards

A risk strip sits at the top of Access Overview, Role paths, Who has access, What they see and Can they?: a few lines, worst first, each with a count, a link and, when it has items, a table that opens in place. A person or role gets one set of checks, an object another. Home shows the account's numbers from one pass over the findings.

## One line (`server.py:1733-1759`)
- `risk(bad, text, n, link, cols, rows)` -> `severity` `bad` | `warn`, and `table` `{cols, rows, total}` with the first `RISK_ROWS` (10) rows, null without items (`server.py:1733-1739`); `ranked()` puts `bad` first and keeps the built order within a tone (`server.py:1758-1759`).
- `more(xs)`: the first `RISK_TOP` (3) names, then `+N` (`server.py:1730`, `1742-1743`).
- `findings_risk(xs, to)`: the findings count per severity and the first 3 short rule names, worst severity first, plus a table Severity / Finding / On; `bad` when any is Critical or High (`server.py:1746-1755`).

## Person or role (`risks_of`, `server.py:1787-1831`; cached per subject by `subject_risks`, `server.py:1780-1784`)

| Line | When | Tone (table and link) |
|---|---|---|
| Is admin role X | a role in `ADMIN` (its `ADMIN_POWER` text) | bad |
| Holds N admin roles: R via F | `admin_paths`, the shortest path per admin role | bad (Admin role, Path) |
| N account privileges | `account_privs` not reached through PUBLIC | bad (Privilege, Path; link: Access > Can run) |
| Reads N sensitive objects unmasked | `seen_counts` (as the Access page counts) | bad (Object, Sensitive columns in clear, "not known" when unread; link: What they see > Column by column) |
| N rule findings (counts): names | findings whose grantee is the subject | bad if Critical / High |
| Default role is admin role X | user's `DEFAULT_ROLE` in `ADMIN` | bad |
| Disabled / Never logged in / Dormant, still holds N roles | `stale(name)` and roles held | warn (Role held) |
| Very broad access | reads >= `BROAD` (25%) and >= `BROAD_MIN` (20) of the account's data objects | warn |
| Secondary roles ALL | `DEFAULT_SECONDARY_ROLES` holds ALL and more than one role held | warn (Granted role) |

- Constants: `server.py:1724-1730`; data object total `data_total()` (`server.py:1762-1763`).

## Object (`object_risks_of`, `server.py:1845-1878`; cached by `object_risks`, `server.py:1838-1842`)
- From the grants, without the Who has access walk, so Can they? stays fast: readers through `READ_PRIVS`, writers through `WRITES`, minus users lacking USAGE on its database or schema (`usage_gaps`) (`server.py:1846-1849`).
- Lines: sensitive columns without masking while someone can read it (bad); granted to PUBLIC (bad when sensitive); people, not service users, who can change a sensitive object (bad); disabled or dormant readers (bad when sensitive); rule findings naming the object; only admin roles reach it (warn); not used in `UNUSED` (90) days yet at least `WIDE` (3) users can read it, from `object_activity()` (warn). Tables: columns without masking, people who can change it, stale readers with status, findings; the other lines have none (`server.py:1852-1877`).

## Home (`home_page`, `server.py:1881-1894`)
- Shared view only for the risk numbers and cards; My access gets its own ladder counts (`server.py:1883-1889`).
- `home_summary()`, once per data set (`server.py:1897-1931`): findings per severity and per rule, distinct people and roles per severity, unmasked sensitive columns (rule 6, first `NAMES`), dormant readers (rule 7), governance KPIs. **Needs attention** (`act_first`): Critical, then High rules, rarest first so a rule with thousands of findings does not bury one with a few, at most `ACT_FIRST` (5), each with its first `NAMES` subjects (`server.py:1917-1921`, `1934`).
- `home_cards()`, once per data set (`server.py:1942-1990`): admin holders by admin role (service users apart, account privilege only counted), stale people by status, users by status and type, roles by kind, objects by type (`TOP_TYPES` 6 + Other), chain depth, biggest schemas and databases (`TOP_BIG` 6), daily queries of the last `DAYS` (60), object activity counts ([object-activity.md](object-activity.md)), and What changed counts only when that diff is already made: Home never compares (`server.py:1985-1990`).

## Tests
- `test_risks` (`test_server.py:1919`): the strip on Access Overview, Role paths, Who has access, What they see and Can they?; every table has 1 to `RISK_ROWS` rows and the linked page lists the same items. `web/src/components/risks.test.tsx`: a line opens its table in place.
